hyperedges.label: Data Flow: RLE Parser -> Patterns -> Engine -> UI

nodes.label: OpenSpec Artifact
nodes.author: openspec
nodes.rationale: Artifacts are the planning documents within a change (proposal.md, spec.md, design.md, tasks.md) managed via a dependency graph with status tracking (done, skipped, ready, blocked).

nodes.label: OpenSpec Change
nodes.author: openspec
nodes.rationale: A change is a named unit of work in OpenSpec containing planning artifacts (proposal, specs, design, tasks) that progress through propose, apply, sync, update, and archive stages.

nodes.label: OpenSpec Store
nodes.author: openspec
nodes.rationale: A store is a standalone OpenSpec repo registered on the machine, selected via --store <id> flag, allowing specs and changes to live outside the current project.

nodes.label: Spec-Driven Schema
nodes.author: openspec
nodes.rationale: The default workflow schema producing proposal, specs (delta), design, and tasks artifacts in dependency order. Custom schemas are also supported.

nodes.label: Fluid Workflow Integration
nodes.author: openspec
nodes.rationale: The apply skill supports an actions-on-a-change model where workflows are not phase-locked. Apply can be invoked before all artifacts are done, after partial implementation, or interleaved with other actions. Implementation can suggest artifact updates fluidly.

nodes.label: Planning Boundary
nodes.author: openspec
nodes.rationale: The propose workflow creates planning artifacts only and never edits project code, even if the triggering request asks to build. Implementation requires an explicit separate apply invocation. This separation prevents accidental code changes during planning.

nodes.label: Delta Spec
nodes.author: openspec
nodes.rationale: A delta spec describes incremental changes to requirements using ADDED, MODIFIED, REMOVED, and RENAMED sections, which are intelligently merged into main specs during sync.

nodes.label: Main Spec
nodes.author: openspec
nodes.rationale: The authoritative spec file for a capability, living under openspec/specs/<capability-path>/spec.md, containing Purpose and Requirements sections with no delta operation headers.

nodes.label: Intelligent Merging
nodes.author: openspec
nodes.rationale: Agent-driven semantic merge preserves existing content not mentioned in the delta, adds new scenarios without copying entire requirements, and uses judgment rather than programmatic overwrite. This is the key design decision enabling the sync workflow.

nodes.label: Bundled Patterns as .rle Files
nodes.rationale: Ship as actual .rle files in priv/patterns/ rather than hardcoded coordinates. Exercises the RLE parser on every load, adding new patterns is just dropping a file.

nodes.label: Mix Escript Distribution
nodes.rationale: Build as escript (mix escript.build) for single-binary distribution. Main entry point invokes Ratatouille.run/2.

nodes.label: MapSet Sparse Grid Representation
nodes.rationale: MapSet of {x,y} tuples chosen over 2D list/array (sparse, memory proportional to alive cells), Map (simpler, no per-cell data), and ETS (overkill for single-process). O(1) membership testing.

nodes.label: Module Structure (Engine, RLE, Patterns, UI.App)
nodes.rationale: Four modules: Engine (stateless pure functions), RLE (parser), Patterns (bundled .rle files from priv/patterns/), UI.App (Ratatouille app with state). Minimal coupling between simulation, parsing, and presentation.

nodes.label: Ratatouille TUI Framework
nodes.rationale: Ratatouille chosen over raw ANSI escape codes (provides Elm-architecture loop, event handling, layout primitives) and direct ExTermbox (higher-level API with no loss). Tick driven by Process.send_after/3.

nodes.label: Simulation Tick via Self-Messaging
nodes.rationale: Process.send_after/3 chosen over separate GenServer (unnecessary complexity) and :timer.send_interval (harder to adjust dynamically). Speed changes simply alter the interval.

nodes.label: Viewport Centering Calculation
nodes.rationale: Compute bounding box of alive cells on pattern load, center viewport. Render at (cell_x - viewport_left, cell_y - viewport_top), clip to bounds.
